resources.string: Shown while a remote command makes the phone ring or vibrate, with a button to stop it.
One notification for each remote command received, executed or refused.
Watchpost is making this phone ring
channel switched off, or remote erase not allowed on the phone
no command passphrase set on the phone
invalid signature (wrong passphrase, or command not issued by you)
sensitive commands blocked for one hour after 5 invalid signatures
"Do not disturb" mutes alarms: vibration and notification only
location collector disabled or without permission
refused by the server: re-enroll or "Reconnect"

Your server can ask this phone to ring, vibrate, locate itself, lock with a message or erase itself — nothing else: no command can change a setting, the policy or the enrollment. Every command received is shown as a notification and in the history below.
Off: the phone no longer contacts the server for commands.
To be measured on your phone: the permanent connection wakes the radio at every keep-alive message from the server (every 2 min).
Command received within seconds. Cost: one connection kept open continuously.
The phone asks whether there are commands at the chosen interval (and on every event upload). In deep sleep, the actual interval may grow longer.

This passphrase is known only to this phone and to you: the server never receives it and can neither lock nor erase this phone without it. You will be asked for it in the console for every sensitive command (lock, clear the message, erase). The phone keeps only a derived key, encrypted.\n\nTwo limits to know. 1) The server sees your signed commands go by: whoever controls it can try passphrases at their own pace. Choose a long, unpredictable passphrase reserved for this use: five or more randomly chosen words, or 16 characters produced by a password manager (12 characters is a minimum, not a guarantee). 2) You type this passphrase into the console, which that same server serves you: a compromised server can learn it at that moment. At the slightest doubt, change the passphrase here — commands already signed become ineffective — and switch off "Allow remote erase".
Not set: lock and erase are refused
To be re-entered: the device identifier changed since
Enroll the device first: the passphrase depends on its identifier.
Passphrase saved. Enter exactly the same one in the console.
Passphrase too easy to guess: it needs at least 6 distinct characters and, without letters, at least 20 digits. Prefer five randomly chosen words.
Passphrase deleted; remote erase is forbidden again.

Disabled by default. When enabled, an "erase" command signed with your passphrase resets the phone to factory state: all data is lost, permanently. Factory reset protection (Google account) and eSIMs are kept.

A command signed with your command passphrase will be able to reset this phone to factory settings, with no other confirmation on the phone. This is irreversible: photos, messages and apps will be lost unless they are backed up elsewhere.

Anyone who knows or finds this passphrase and controls your server can therefore erase this phone: only enable this setting with a long, unpredictable passphrase reserved for this use.

To confirm, type ERASE.
No message set by a command.
Locking and displaying a message require Watchpost to be Device Owner.
